title: A Alibi for the Parish
premise: Xanthe Yarrow, a concierge in the fading seaside parish of St. Merrin's, recognizes the drowned stranger pulled from the harbor — not by face, but by the clothes, stolen item by item from Xanthe's own closet. The dead man turns out to be connected to a drowning twenty years ago, ruled accidental, in which Xanthe's found family — the parish regulars who took them in as a runaway — all played some part. As Xanthe investigates, memory and loyalty war: the 'closed' case was closed by kindness as much as by lies. In the end Xanthe must expose the true killer — the parish's beloved harbormaster, who drowned a blackmailer to protect the secret that the first death was his fault — and choose to stay with the family that lied to them, rebuilt on truth rather than silence.
about_author: Gideon Eriksen is the pen name of a former night-desk clerk who spent a decade watching strangers check in and out of coastal hotels, collecting the small betrayals people confess at 3 a.m. They write mysteries about places that remember, and people who wish they didn't.

chapters.title: The Tide Keeps Its Own
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. A routine dawn shift at the Saltgull Hotel is broken by sirens: a body in the harbor. Xanthe recognizes the dead man's cardigan, scarf, and shoes — their own, taken from their staff closet. The chapter establishes Xanthe's habit of noticing everything and their careful, self-contained life. Emotional beat: unease curdling into violation.

chapters.title: Clothes Without a Man
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Detective Inspector Rhoan Keswick interviews Xanthe, who admits the clothes are theirs but cannot say when they were taken. Flashback seeds: Xanthe arrived in St. Merrin's as a runaway teenager and was taken in by the parish regulars. Emotional beat: the horror of being known too well by someone unseen.

chapters.title: The Regulars
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Xanthe visits the parish's found family: landlady Odile, churchwarden Bram, and aging harbormaster Silas Fen, who taught Xanthe the tides. All offer comfort; all are oddly unsurprised by death. Emotional beat: warmth shadowed by the sense that everyone is performing calm.

chapters.title: A Name in the Guest Book
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. The victim is identified: Tobias Wrenne, a journalist who checked in under a false name two weeks ago. Xanthe remembers him — he asked strange questions about the parish, and about 'the boy who drowned.' Emotional beat: the past knocking politely, then kicking.

chapters.title: What the Water Gave Back
chapters.summary: Silas's POV, twenty years earlier. A young man, Callum, drowns off the breakwater during a storm; Silas was on the water that night and saw more than he reported. The inquest rules it accidental. Emotional beat: guilt worn smooth as sea glass, but not gone.

chapters.title: Everyone Swore It Was Closed
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. When Xanthe mentions Callum's name, the room goes cold. Odile warns them to leave it; Bram quotes scripture about dead things staying buried. Xanthe realizes the whole parish agreed, once, never to speak of it. Emotional beat: belonging revealed as a contract with fine print.

chapters.title: The Missing Fortnight
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Xanthe reconstructs Wrenne's stay from ledgers, receipts, and staff gossip: he interviewed Odile, photographed the breakwater, and met someone at the salt sheds the night he died. Emotional beat: the concierge's gift — reading strangers — finally turned toward a corpse.

chapters.title: Odile's Locked Room
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Xanthe finds Wrenne's notes hidden in Odile's spare room: clippings suggesting Callum's drowning was no accident, and a list of parish names with sums beside them — payments, or blackmail. Emotional beat: suspicion turning toward the people who raised them.

chapters.title: Bram's Confession of Small Sins
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. The churchwarden admits he helped cover up that Callum had been drinking with parish men that night — a lie of protection, he insists, not guilt. He points Xanthe toward the salt sheds. Emotional beat: a good man explaining how goodness becomes complicity.

chapters.title: Salt Sheds, Low Tide
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. In the sheds Xanthe finds a rotted rope and a boat hook matching a scar described in the old inquest. Someone has been keeping the evidence — not destroying it. Footprints, still fresh, lead toward the harbor. Emotional beat: the case breathing again.

chapters.title: The Second Alibi
chapters.summary: Keswick's POV. The DI works the murder independently: Wrenne's editor reveals he was blackmailing several St. Merrin's families over the old drowning, and every suspect has an alibi — too neat, too mutual, as if rehearsed. Emotional beat: institutional patience grinding against a wall of communal silence.

chapters.title: Odile Breaks
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Confronted, Odile confesses she paid Wrenne to go away — she was protecting Xanthe, she says, from learning what their parish did. She saw Silas's boat out the night Wrenne died and said nothing. Emotional beat: love confessed as a form of lying.

chapters.title: What Silas Taught Me About Tides
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Xanthe works the tide tables and realizes the body could only have been placed where it was found by someone who knew the harbor's currents intimately — a shortlist of one. The mentor-shaped hole in the theory terrifies them. Emotional beat: dawning grief ahead of proof.

chapters.title: The Night Callum Died
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Full flashback: Silas, drunk and furious that Callum was courting his daughter, followed him onto the breakwater; a shove, a slip — he has never let himself decide which. He let the sea take the blame. Emotional beat: self-deception cracking under twenty years of weight.

chapters.title: Daughter of the Harbor
chapters.summary: Maren Fen's POV. Silas's daughter, who left the parish years ago, returns quietly and tells Xanthe her father's rages, her fear of him, and that Wrenne contacted her first. She gives Xanthe a letter Wrenne sent — proof, if Silas is guilty. Emotional beat: two damaged people choosing truth over inherited silence.

chapters.title: The Alibi for the Parish
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Xanthe assembles the communal lie: each regular gave the others alibis for the murder night, a mutual shelter built the same way they once buried Callum's death. The title's meaning lands — the parish's real alibi is its own kindness. Emotional beat: heartbreak at how love and cover-up share a shape.

chapters.title: Storm Warning
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Xanthe tells Keswick everything; Keswick admits the evidence is suggestive but not damning, and warns that Silas will know who talked. That night, Xanthe's room at the Saltgull is searched — and the Wrenne letter is gone. Emotional beat: the hunter realizing he is also prey.

chapters.title: The Breakwater at Flood
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV, climax part one. A forged note lures Xanthe onto the breakwater in a rising storm — the same spot, the same weather, twenty years later. Silas appears, not to kill, but to finally be witnessed: he confesses everything to the one person he thinks of as his own. Emotional beat: terror braided with a terrible tenderness.

chapters.title: What the Sea Was Owed
chapters.summary: Silas's POV, climax part two. Silas, half-drowned by the storm he misjudged, clings to the breakwater that took Callum. Xanthe must choose: let the sea settle the account, or haul him back to face a human court. Xanthe pulls him out. Emotional beat: mercy as the harder, better choice.

chapters.title: The Inquest, Reopened
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Silas confesses formally; both deaths are laid before the law. The parish fractures — some call Xanthe a traitor, others finally exhale. Keswick closes the case with the truth instead of the old kindness. Emotional beat: justice arriving without absolution.

chapters.title: What We Keep
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Aftermath: Odile and Bram, ashamed but present, help Xanthe sort the closet, the ledgers, the past. Xanthe learns Wrenne's stolen clothes were taken by Odile to destroy — she was the closet thief, trying to sever the link. Forgiveness begins, incomplete and real. Emotional beat: grief settling into something livable.

chapters.title: Checking In
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV, coda. Months later, a nervous young runaway arrives at the Saltgull's desk with no luggage and nowhere to go. Xanthe, who notices everything, notices that — and gives her a room, the way the parish once gave them one. The tide comes in, ordinary and clean. Emotional beat: belonging chosen again, eyes open.
